title: Fast Ships Swing Wide
headline: Ships fly themselves through three growing laps against reshuffled rivals; the player's decisions are on the pre-race board and at one pit stop per lap — how the ship treats bends, what the navigation system aims for, what shapes the course, and what to spend or hold.

questions.question: Does any in-race tap survive, or is the race auto-only with the thumb at the board and pit stops?
questions.why: Decides whether abilities are purely automatic or a single override tap remains, which sets what the race asks of the player.

questions.question: Fixed groups for three laps, or reshuffled each lap as the note asks?
questions.why: Changes what a heat is: one three-lap duel scored as a race, or three lap-races summed. Both readers say the reshuffle version leaves unstated what a ship keeps between laps and whether nine ships share one loop or three.

questions.question: How does a group fill when the set cutoff leaves a survivor count not divisible by three?
questions.why: A short group, a game-run pace ship, or a cutoff that always leaves a multiple of three are different systems with different fairness.

questions.question: Do splits carry into rivals' courses the way fixtures do?
questions.why: A rival's permanent split can reshape your whole heat; whether course works are shared like fixtures or private-until-grouped decides how much course one purchase controls.

nextRound: The notes all landed and the idea survives, and both readers land on one gap the notes opened: reshuffling rivals every lap turns a heat into three separate races, and the document never says what a ship keeps across a lap boundary, whether nine ships run one shared loop or three, or how long a heat is. Answer that first — a paragraph of what carries and what resets — because everything downstream depends on it. Then the smaller asks: a one-line verdict after each lap naming the plan, the stat and the draw that cost you; a precedence rule between declaration, nav goal and corner plan; one trigger line per ability; and whether a fork overshoot lands wide or on the path, and whether an involuntary branch breaks the Long Line. The swing is still invisible — the owner has not spoken to it yet, and both readers keep raising it.
gaps: Per-lap reshuffle makes each lap a separate race and nothing says what a ship keeps across the boundary or whether nine ships share one loop
The swing is invisible — carried over from round 5, still not addressed by the owner
Abilities have no stated triggers, so reaction time has nothing to be measured from
No precedence between a declaration, the nav goal and the corner plan when they disagree at a bend
